# The Swiss theme

Designed 2026-10-17. A fourth theme, beside the default, the retro and the cosy: the app as a Swiss poster. A strict grid, black and white and a single red, no shadow nor rounding, the figures large. First of the three themes kept after the cosy (Swiss, then Ink and wash, then Metro signage): coded first because it is the simplest, its flat pieces serving as a start for Ink.

Mock-up (screen of a zone): `docs/theme-tracks.html`, "Swiss" card.

## What is decided

All the lines of 2026-10-17, in the order of the list of `docs/THEMES.md`.

1. **The register**: an off-white background, black ink, a single red. A tile is a thick black line above its content, without a frame. A huge screen title, aligned left; the group titles in spaced capitals, without a rule of their own: the tiles' line beneath holds the line; the tool names in small capitals; the figures featured. It is neither warm, nor decorative, nor textured, nor raised.
   - **The red is for the app's signals**: the floating button, the waiting mark, the interaction card, the danger button. A chart's goal stays in ink, dashed: the core's drawing does not tell it apart from the other lines. The full solids are the theme's: the ink, or the red for what it names.
   - **The user's colours** (tags, icon colour) are only **small square marks**, never a solid; the only exception, a Chart's series (line 10). The icon-only tile is a solid of ink, never of its colour.
2. **What it draws itself**: everything, dialogs and date and time selectors included, nothing taken from the default theme nor Material (no ripple, no tinted surface, no elevation).
3. **The font**: Archivo alone (SIL Open Font License 1.1, without a reserved name), copied into `third_party/archivo/`; a script `scripts/make_archivo_fonts.py` draws from it four fixed weights at normal width (`wdth` 100): 400 the text, 600 the names and labels, 800 the group titles, 900 the screen titles and the figures; from its italic, copied beside, 400 and 600, for the italic of a read text. It covers Windows-1252, the arrows, `≤ ≥ ≠ ≈ − ×` (measured 2026-10-17); it lacks the narrow no-break space (U+202F), which the script adds (an empty space of one eighth of an em, the thin space of French typography), and `✓`, left to Android's fallback: only the command lines of an AI message write it, with `✗` (`ChatComponents`). Fixed-width figures (`tnum`) everywhere.
4. **The palettes** (OKLCH, lightness · saturation · hue; contrast aimed at 4.5):
   - light: off-white background `#f2f0eb` (0.955 · 0.007 · 89), ink `#111` (16.6), secondary `#555` (6.6), red at lightness 0.52 and saturation 0.202 (5.4 in text on the background, 4.56 at the worst of the shifts, the worst at 120°; the mock-up's `#e8331c` only held 3.75), white text on the red; the tag squares at lightness 0.60, at least 3 on the background (a mark, not a text);
   - dark: background `#141414`, off-white ink (16.2), secondary `#a8a6a0` (7.6), red `#ff4a33` (5.5 on the background), background text on the red (white only holds 3.3 there);
   - the rail of a gauge, a neutral grey: `#d4d1c9` light, `#3a3936` dark;
   - the hue turns only the red, the rest being without saturation; states and tags kept. `SwissPaletteTest` holds each contrast in both modes and at each shift by 15° steps: a shift under 4.5 lowers the red's lightness for all.
5. **The geometry**: a step of 8 dp; `UI.Space` XS 4, S 8, M 16, L 24, XL 32, `EDGE` 16. Square cells, 12 dp between two columns, 16 between two rows, left empty by the grid, the grid of at most 480 dp. A tile has no side margin: its content starts at the left edge of its line, 8 dp under it, on the same vertical as the titles; the icon-only tile keeps 8 dp around. The finger target at 48 dp, the drawing able to be smaller. `drawingUnit` 1.
6. **The size**: Android's text size followed, for the text alone; the step (0 to 3) enlarges everything by ×1, ×1.12, ×1.25 and ×1.4 (step 0 = the mock-up), except the spacings, the edge margin and the grid's gaps, fixed in dp, the lines rounded to the whole pixel. The screen title (46 sp) goes to the next line, cut at the syllables; past two lines, its size comes down until it fits in two, never below a group title's.
7. **The components**:
   - frames: the tile, an ink line of 3 dp on top; the card (variable, routine, line of a list), a hairline of 1 dp on top; the dialog and the floating window, a rectangle of the background with a hairline of 1 dp all round and an ink bar of 6 dp on top, on the screen veiled in black at 50%, which darkens in both modes (an ink veil would lighten the dark, seen on the bench); the user's bubble, an ink solid pushed right with the background's text, the AI's without a bubble, the text aligned left under a hairline of 1 dp; the interaction card, a red line of 3 dp on top;
   - buttons: primary in an ink solid, the background's label in spaced capitals 600; secondary in an ink outline of 2 dp; tertiary and neutral, the label alone underlined 1 dp; danger in a red outline of 2 dp, red label; disabled, the drawing of its type in the rail's grey and the label in secondary ink; on in an ink solid; icon-only, the icon without a frame in 48 dp; the floating button, a solid red square of 56 dp, the icon white in light, of the background in dark;
   - input: the field without a box, a hairline of 1 dp under the text, 2 dp at focus, the label above in small capitals in secondary ink, the error to the hairline and the message in the state colour; the selection, the same field and a chevron, its menu a panel like the dialog, the chosen option in a solid; the box, a 20 dp square with a 2 dp outline, ticked a full square without a tick; the switch, a 44 × 24 dp rectangle with a 2 dp outline and a square thumb, on full of ink, the thumb right on the background; yes / no, two segments stuck together, the chosen in a solid; the slider, a 2 dp rail and a 4 × 24 dp vertical bar, the value above in bold figures; the gauge, a 6 dp bar, grey rail, filling in ink, never red even full; the hue band in saturated colours, the choice in a 2 dp rectangle; the tabs in capitals, the chosen in ink underlined 3 dp, the others in secondary ink;
   - marks: the tag, an 8 dp square of its colour before its text in ink; the separator, a hairline of 1 dp; the group titles in capitals 800 spaced 0.10 em, never cut in the middle of a word, without the mock-up's red numbering (the theme does not know a group's rank, and adding it to the contract for a decoration is not worth its cost); the handle, two ink bars of 2 dp; the waiting mark, a red square at the top right corner with a "!" 900 of the background; the coloured icon, the icon in ink and a 6 dp square of its colour at its bottom right corner, the same place without colour; the textures, orthogonal patterns (hairlines of 1 dp, square dots, gridding) set on the 8 dp step, in ink and faint, on the tile under its line and over the whole background of a textured page (`PageGround`, `docs/THEMES.md`);
   - waiting: the loading, an ink bar of 2 dp that runs from left to right; the AI thinking, three ink squares of 8 dp that fill one after the other;
   - messages: the toast, an ink solid at the bottom over the width less `EDGE`, background text; the snackbar, the same, its action in capitals underlined of the background;
   - date and time: the date in the dialog's frame, month and year in capitals 900 between two chevrons, the days' initials in small secondary capitals, the days in figures aligned on 7 columns without a circle, the chosen in a full square, today underlined 3 dp; the time, two counters, hours and minutes in figures 900 at the screen title's size separated by ":", each between two square − and + buttons with a 2 dp outline, without a dial;
   - page header and mark: the page's icon in 24 dp in ink above the giant title, the subtitle in small secondary capitals under it; the app's mark, the icon's monochrome layer (`make_launcher_icon.py`) in ink;
   - the bar of a selected text: an ink solid, its words in capitals 600 of the background separated by hairlines of 1 dp of the background, a touched word inverted.
8. **The touch and the movement**: a clean cut. The pressed element inverts, ink and background exchanged, without transition nor ripple; an appearance is a 120 ms linear fade, without growing nor sliding, and closes at once; the lifted element takes an ink outline of 2 dp and shifts 4 dp up and left, without a shadow, and falls into place at once. Animations cut in Android: the fade disappears, the rest being already instantaneous.
9. **The icons**: Lucide (`LUCIDE`), as is.
10. **The charts**: drawn by the theme (`SwissDrawing`). The colours the user gives to the series are kept, the only exception to the small marks; solids without rounding, strokes with square tips, square dots, the axes in hairlines of 1 dp, the labels in aligned figures; the ink levels in ink, the secondary and the rail's grey.
11. **The edit mode of the grid**: a cell, a square with a hairline of 1 dp in ink at 20%; the chosen tile, the lifted tile of line 8.
12. **The sound register**: dry and short, clicks and ticks without a note (a switch, a stapler), the opposite of the cosy's round sounds; to look for in click, tick, switch and toggle of Kenney's Interface Sounds and UI Audio. Chosen by ear: `sounds-choice.json`.
13. **The texts**: name "Swiss"; tagline "Like a Swiss poster: a strict grid, black and white and a single red, the numbers large, its own sounds". No palette name.

## What is coded

`themes/swiss/`: the palette (`SwissPalette`, its numbers in `palettes.json`, set on the bench `./run themes`, "Swiss · palettes", seen and approved 2026-10-17), the sizes and the font by step (`SwissSize`), the pressed element, the fade, the lifted element and the strokes (`SwissPieces`), the charts (`SwissDrawing`), each contract component (`SwissTheme`), the textures' cells (`textures/`, on the 8 step, with square tips). `SwissPaletteTest` holds the two palettes' contrasts at each 15° shift. Chosen in Settings › Interface, under the name "Swiss".

What the code made precise among the decisions:
- A tile's or a page background's texture is drawn in ink, without the icon's colour, which the core would give to the pattern.
- The cards and the conversation's messages are full, of the screen's background: a page background pattern never passes under a long text (`PageGround`).
- The page title comes down, past two lines, to a dialog title's size (22 sp): a group title's (12 sp) was too small for a title.
- The veil behind a dialog is Android's (black), the floating window being common to all themes.
- A series' dots keep the shape the chart gives them: it can tell two series apart.
- After the first pass on the phone (2026-10-19): a tile's name aligned left after its icon, which the theme decides (`tileNameAlign`); a section's header without a rule, the space under its title given back so that it sits closer to its tiles than to the previous ones; a tile name or a group title cut between two words only, spaced 0.10 em instead of 0.16, so that a word of twelve capitals fits on a two-cell tile up to step 1; past that, a word longer than the tile still gets cut.

## What stays open

- The textures' tones are the default theme's, copied: to set on the textures bench (`./run themes`).
- The sounds, on the phone: their level by ear.
